subject: maths
question: A set of data presented in the form of a frequency distribution table with class intervals and their respective frequencies had a mode of 48.5. The lower boundary of the modal class was 46.5; the frequency of the modal class was 34; the frequency of the class interval just preceding the modal class was 32 and the frequency of the class interval just succeeding the modal class was 25. What was the width of the modal class?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference between Mode and Lower limit = (f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) × h

48.5 − 46.5 = (34 − 32) ÷ (2 × 34 − 32 − 25) × h

2 = (2 ÷ 11) × h

h = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mode (Mₒ) = 48.5

Lower boundary of modal class (l) = 46.5

Frequency of modal class (f₁) = 34

Frequency of preceding class (f₀) = 32

Frequency of succeeding class (f₂) = 25

**Formula Used:**

Mode = l + [ (f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) ] × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/26f8b4f2a73404a96a90d2bb7de6e66512e8ebd6ffbe43cd3da4be60ed367f21.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 48.5 = 46.5 + [ (34 − 32) ÷ (2 × 34 − 32 − 25) ] × h

⇒ 48.5 − 46.5 = [ 2 ÷ (68 − 57) ] × h

⇒ 2 = (2 ÷ 11) × h

⇒ 2 × 11 = 2h

⇒ 22 = 2h

⇒ h = 22 ÷ 2

⇒ h = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median for Grouped Data

Median = l + [ (N/2 − cf) ÷ f ] × h, where l is lower limit of median class and cf is cumulative frequency of preceding class.

Empirical Relationship

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean. This formula is used for moderately skewed distributions.

Mean for Grouped Data (Direct Method)

Mean = Σfᵢxᵢ ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ is the class mark (mid-value) of each interval.</p
